business_scope.primary_industry_name: Manufacture of High-Voltage Power Transformers and Switchgear

Agreement between the Government of the People's Republic of China and the Government of the Republic of France on the Reciprocal Encouragement and Protection of Investments

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering Law of the People's Republic of China (effective 1 January 2025, as amended 31 December 2024); Measures for the Administration of Beneficial Owner Information of Enterprises issued by the People's Bank of China (PBOC) and the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) under Order No. 3 of 2024, effective 1 November 2024; Regulations on Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing; Provisions on the Registration and Record-Filing of Foreign-Invested Enterprises; Provisions on Information Reporting by Companies and other AML/CFT implementing rules.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (Business License) of the foreign investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or other competent corporate registrar in the foreign shareholder's country of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If the document originates in a Hague Apostille Convention member state, the document must be notarized (if required by origin law) and then sealed with a Hague Apostille by the designated competent authority in that state; no consular legalization is to be added. If the document originates in a non-member state, the notarized document must be authenticated by the origin country's Ministry of Foreign Affairs and then consularized by the Chinese Embassy or Consulate in that country; no apostille is to be added. The two paths are parallel and mutually exclusive.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing for the foreign investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Same corporate registrar or competent authority in the foreign investor's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille member state: notarize if needed, then obtain only a Hague Apostille from the designated competent authority; no consular legalization. Non-member state: notarize, authenticate through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs or equivalent, then complete consular legalization at the Chinese Embassy/Consulate; no apostille. Never chain apostille and consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution or Power of Attorney authorizing the formation of the China WFOE
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the foreign investor company, notarized before a licensed notary public in the origin country
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille member state: notarization followed solely by Hague Apostille; destination authorities will reject if consular legalization is attempted afterwards. Non-member state: notarization, then Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication, then Chinese consular legalization. The two routes are separate and must not be combined.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (or equivalent constitutional document) of the foreign investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign investor company as adopted and certified by its registered agent or competent registrar
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille member state: issue Hague Apostille only after any required domestic notarization; no consular legalization. Non-member state: notarize, have the document authenticated by the local designated authority, and then obtain Chinese consular legalization; apostille is unavailable and must not be substituted.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter from the foreign investor's principal settlement bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign investor's relationship bank, signed by an authorized bank officer
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille member state: notarize the bank officer's signature if necessary, then obtain a Hague Apostille; no consular legalization. Non-member state: notarize the signature, then authenticate through the origin country's Ministry of Foreign Affairs, then Chinese consular legalization; no apostille. Parallel and mutually exclusive only.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: The due diligence layer must screen all shareholder directors and ultimate beneficial owners against UN Security Council sanctions lists, US OFAC SDN list, EU consolidated list, and the PRC Ministry of Public Security publications. Each UBO must complete an enhanced source-of-wealth questionnaire whenever a listed country connection, PEP status, or high-risk jurisdiction is determined. PEP identification covers current and former politically exposed persons, close associates, and family members, with approval required by a senior AML compliance officer. Red flags must be escalated to the PBOC filing agent within 24 hours, and all screening evidence must be retained for at least five years after the relationship ends.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) Enterprise Registration and Name Reservation Online Public Service Platform
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The WFOE must have a registered name in Simplified Chinese characters only, using the four-tier formula: administrative division, distinctive trade name, industry characteristic, and organization form. Pinyin transliteration, if any, must be exact Hanyu Pinyin and is recorded as an alias, not as the primary registered name. The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered enterprise name in the same or similar industry nationwide.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant must request the local SAMR bureau to state the refusal grounds in writing within 5 working days. The applicant may then submit a formal re-examination application to the same bureau within 15 days, followed by an administrative reconsideration petition to the next higher SAMR within 60 days of the rejection notice. If the administrative reconsideration is unsuccessful, judicial review may be initiated within 6 months under the Administrative Litigation Law, with supporting evidence of trademark rights and industry scope.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: An actual physical office address is mandatory for the WFOE's business license; virtual offices, commercial mailboxes and co-working addresses without a valid lease are rejected by SAMR and by the tax authority for VAT and corporate income tax registration. For ISIC 2710 / NAICS 335311 manufacture of high-voltage power transformers and switchgear, banks and the local commerce bureau also require proof of a real operating site, usually production or R&D premises, and will not accept a mail-forwarding address as registered office or commercial substance.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: valid lease agreement, site signage, staffing presence, actual power transformers manufacturing equipment, utility bills, tax filings, social insurance payroll, environmental impact assessment and fire safety approval. Quantified risk: high for a manufacturing project; estimated 65-70% chance of an on-site inspection by SAMR or the municipal tax bureau within the first 12 months, and annual renewals in the following years.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Government name reservation and WFOE business license registration filing fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) local municipal office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff zero; official registration fee is waived for electronic filings in most Chinese municipalities

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of foreign investor identity documents and Hague apostille or consular legalization of the 5-instrument bundle
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Foreign notary public, origin-country Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and Chinese Embassy/Consulate as applicable
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official government fee schedules plus prevailing notary market benchmark for a 5-document package

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified Chinese translation of all foreign corporate documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Local registered translation company and Chinese notary office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market standard of RMB 200-500 per 1,000 Chinese characters plus notarization statutory fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO register filing and AML/CFT onboarding compliance review
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: PBOC and SAMR joint beneficial owner information system via licensed filing agent
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Filing itself bears no government fee; the quoted amount is the licensed agent and AML compliance service fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: WFOE articles of association drafting, notarization and PRC legal opinion
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark per the PRC price bureau guidance and prevailing city-level legal fee ranges

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office lease verification and commercial substance due diligence
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Commercial landlord or real estate agent in the target Chinese municipality
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market rental rates plus due diligence service benchmark; no set government tariff

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2018 Amendment), Articles 23-30 (Incorporation), Articles 33-37 (Articles of Association), Articles 44-46 (Board of Directors), Articles 49-50 (Legal Representative), and the Foreign Investment Law (2019) and its Implementing Regulations
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) – Enterprise Registration Department (local counterpart: Municipal Administration for Market Regulation)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Establishment Registration of a Foreign-Invested Enterprise (外商投资企业设立登记申请书) and the Articles of Association (公司章程)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a WFOE under PRC law; however, the registered capital must be fully subscribed and paid in accordance with the schedule in the Articles of Association (typically within 30 years for manufacturing). Capital contributions must be injected via a foreign exchange capital account (FDI) and verified by the designated bank. No escrow account is required, but the capital must be paid in within the agreed timeline to avoid penalties.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTION OF THE FIRST MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME] (the 'Company'), a wholly foreign-owned enterprise incorporated under the laws of the People's Republic of China.

The undersigned, being the duly appointed directors of the Company, convened at the registered office on [date] at [time]. The meeting was called in accordance with the Articles of Association and the Company Law of the People's Republic of China. The following resolutions were proposed and unanimously adopted:

1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION: RESOLVED, that the registered capital of the Company be fixed at [amount] RMB, divided into [number] shares of [par value] each, and that the sole shareholder (the foreign parent) subscribes to all such shares. The capital shall be paid in accordance with the schedule set forth in the Articles of Association, with the initial contribution to be made within 90 days of issuance of the business license, and the balance within the statutory period. The Board authorizes the Legal Representative to open a foreign exchange capital account with a designated bank for the receipt of the capital contribution.

2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION: RESOLVED, that the Company shall open corporate bank accounts with [Bank Name] and that the following persons are authorized as signatories: [Name] (Chairman), [Name] (General Manager), and [Name] (Finance Officer). Any two signatures shall be required for transactions exceeding RMB [threshold]. The Board authorizes the execution of all necessary banking resolutions and mandates.

3. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION: RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company be established at [Location], and that the Board authorizes the execution of a lease agreement and the filing of the address with the State Administration for Market Regulation.

4. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS: RESOLVED, that the following persons be appointed to the following offices: [Name] as Chairman of the Board and Legal Representative; [Name] as General Manager; [Name] as Supervisor (or, if a supervisory board is required, the members thereof). The Legal Representative is authorized to represent the Company in all dealings with government authorities and third parties.

5. GENERAL AUTHORIZATION: RESOLVED, that the officers of the Company be and are hereby authorized to execute all documents, make all filings, and obtain all necessary approvals to effectuate the incorporation, registration, and licensing of the Company, including but not limited to the procurement of the business license, tax registration, and industrial licenses.

This resolution is effective immediately and shall remain in full force until revoked by a subsequent resolution of the Board.

Dated this [day] day of [month], [year].

[Signature of Directors]

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-Approval and Reservation of Company Name
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) – Enterprise Name Registration System (online portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an application for name pre-approval via the SAMR online system. Provide the proposed Chinese and English names, business scope, and shareholder details. The name must comply with the Provisions on Enterprise Name Registration. The system will check for conflicts with existing enterprises and trademarks. Upon approval, the name is reserved for six months. Ensure the name reflects the business scope and does not contain prohibited terms. Submit the required dossiers and obtain the Name Approval Certificate.
required_dossiers: Copy of the foreign investor's business registration certificate (notarized and legalized)
Power of attorney for the local agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, the applicant may submit a new name or provide a letter of consent from the conflicting enterprise. The system will indicate the reason for rejection; correct and resubmit within 10 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Notarization of Incorporation Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public Office (in the investor's home country) and local SAMR (for preliminary review)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Articles of Association, the Application for Establishment Registration, and the list of directors and supervisors. The foreign investor's identity documents must be notarized by a notary in the home country and legalized by the Chinese embassy or consulate (or apostilled if applicable). All documents must be in Chinese or accompanied by a certified Chinese translation. Submit the complete set to the local SAMR for preliminary review to ensure compliance with the Foreign Investment Law and Company Law.
required_dossiers: Notarized and legalized certificate of incorporation of the foreign investor
Bank reference letter of the foreign investor
Articles of Association (signed by all shareholders)
List of directors, supervisors, and legal representative
Lease agreement for the registered office
Power of attorney for the local agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If documents are incomplete, SAMR will issue a notice of deficiencies. Correct and resubmit within 10 days. If notarization is insufficient, re-notarize and legalize the documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Incorporation Application and Issuance of Business License
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) – Enterprise Registration Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the formal application package with the local SAMR, including the Name Approval Certificate, Articles of Association, lease agreement, and all notarized documents. The SAMR will review the application for legal compliance. Upon approval, the SAMR issues the Business License (营业执照), which includes the unified social credit code and serves as the legal proof of incorporation. The license must be collected in person or via authorized agent.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is rejected, respond to SAMR's queries within 15 days. If the business scope includes restricted industries, obtain prior approval from the Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) or other relevant authorities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Registrations (Tax, Social Insurance, and Foreign Exchange)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA), Social Insurance Bureau, and State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 10 days of obtaining the business license, register with the tax authority for a tax identification number (TIN) and tax registration. Register with the social insurance bureau for employee contributions. Open a foreign exchange capital account with a designated bank and complete the FDI registration with SAFE. If the company will engage in import/export, register with the customs authority. Ensure all registrations are completed to avoid penalties.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax registration is delayed, pay late fees. For SAFE registration, ensure the capital injection is reported within the required period. If customs registration is needed, submit the application promptly.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Industrial and Environmental Licensing for Manufacturing Operations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Ecology and Environment (MEE) – local Environmental Protection Bureau; Municipal Emergency Management Bureau (for Civil Defense)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: For the manufacture of transformers (ISIC 2710), obtain the Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) approval. Depending on the scale, a full EIA report or a registration form may be required. Submit the EIA to the local EPB for review. Additionally, obtain a fire safety certificate from the local Fire and Rescue Department after inspection of the premises. If the product falls under the Compulsory Certification (CCC) catalog, obtain the CCC certificate. Ensure compliance with occupational safety standards.
required_dossiers: Fire safety design review and acceptance certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the EIA is rejected, revise the report and resubmit. For fire safety, rectify any deficiencies and re-inspect. If the CCC certificate is required, engage a certified testing body and submit the application.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT) and local Municipal Administration for Market Regulation (for production licenses)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Production License for Electrical Equipment (or Compulsory Certification (CCC) for specific transformer products)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Ecology and Environment (MEE) – local Environmental Protection Bureau
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Full EIA Report (Category A) for transformer manufacturing due to potential oil and chemical emissions; if the facility is small-scale, an Environmental Registration (Category B) may apply.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharge must meet GB 3838-2002 (Integrated Wastewater Discharge Standard) with COD ≤ 100 mg/L, BOD ≤ 30 mg/L, SS ≤ 70 mg/L. VOC emissions must comply with GB 37831-2019 (Emission Standard of Air Pollutants for Volatile Organic Compounds) with non-methane total hydrocarbons ≤ 60 mg/m3. Hazardous waste (e.g., transformer oil) must be handled by licensed entities and stored in compliance with GB 18597-2001.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate from the local Fire and Rescue Department (Civil Defense) after structural inspection, including fire extinguishers, emergency exits, and fire alarm systems. Occupational safety clearance from the local Emergency Management Bureau, ensuring compliance with the Work Safety Law and GB/T 45001-2020 (Occupational Health and Safety Management).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) of the People's Republic of China; principal compliance portal is the national Electronic Tax Bureau (e-Tax) at etax.chinatax.gov.cn, supplemented by the China International Trade Single Window for customs and export procedures.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Name pre-approval and incorporation with the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) via the National Enterprise Registration Service Platform; no minimum capital is required for a WFOE limited-liability company. Step 2: SAMR issues the Business License and assigns the 18-character Unified Social Credit Code (USCC), which is the statutory Tax Identification Number (TIN) for the WFOE; no separate TIN certificate is issued. Step 3: Complete tax registration and taxpayer confirmation in the STA Electronic Tax Bureau within 30 days of the Business License date; the incorporation record is automatically shared with STA. Tax details include the competent tax authority, legal representative, tax supervisor, accounting standards, and payroll declarations. Step 4: Activate VAT invoice quota and Fully Digitalized E-Invoice (FDEI) issuance capacity; submit the VAT general taxpayer election if annual taxable sales exceed CNY 5,000,000 or if the WFOE elects general taxpayer status to claim input-VAT credits. Step 5: Report bank deposit accounts through the Electronic Tax Bureau and complete social insurance registrations. For a foreign non-resident enterprise without a Chinese establishment, the STA issues a Non-Resident Taxpayer Identification Number or permits the Chinese payer or withholding agent to register and withhold on its behalf; this does not apply to the WFOE, which is a resident-taxable entity.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None for US-style check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch elections; the only relevant statutory election is the VAT classification choice under STA Announcement 2018 No. 33: a newly formed WFOE may elect small-scale taxpayer status if expected annual taxable sales do not exceed CNY 5,000,000, or elect general taxpayer status voluntarily; no other entity-level elections exist.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under the PRC Interim Regulation on Value-Added Tax and the STA VAT implementation rules.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CNY 5,000,000 annual VAT taxable sales (mandatory general taxpayer registration threshold); every newly incorporated WFOE is VAT-registered at inception through the SAMR/STA data link, with small-scale taxpayer treatment available below the threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: China mandates issuance through the STA Electronic Invoice Service Platform, using Fully Digitalized E-Invoices (FDEI) with near-real-time transmission of invoice data to the STA tax-control system. Digital invoices carry an STA anti-fraud digital stamp and QR code, enabling automatic verification and clearance. Large and high-volume taxpayers integrate through STA-approved API solutions (Enterprise Direct Link) for automated issuance and reporting. Physical tax-control-device stamping is being phased out in favor of the electronic fiscal platform. For export sales, the WFOE must issue an export ordinary VAT invoice or FDEI and link it to the customs declaration and foreign-exchange receipt through the China International Trade Single Window and SAFE systems.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: The WFOE may apply the 0% export VAT rate to manufactured solid-state transformers where: (1) the goods physically leave PRC customs territory under an export customs declaration; (2) title and risk transfer to a non-resident buyer; (3) the WFOE is a VAT general taxpayer with a complete input-VAT credit chain; (4) export proceeds are repatriated to a PRC-designated bank and reported under SAFE trade-in-foreign-exchange monitoring; and (5) the customs declaration, export invoice, bill of lading, contract, and bank receipt are mutually consistent. Production enterprises satisfying the criteria use the export exemption-credit-refund method, under which output VAT is zero-rated and residual input VAT is refunded.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Export Goods Customs Declaration (Customs Manifest / Bill of Export) generated through the China International Trade Single Window and bearing the 18-digit customs declaration number
Ocean Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical export movement
Commercial Invoice issued by the WFOE in the name of the foreign buyer
Export sales contract or purchase order
Bank Foreign Exchange Collection Voucher / inward remittance advice from a PRC-designated bank
SAFE Electronic Export Proceeds Verification Record (the Chinese statutory equivalent of an Inward Remittance Certificate; China does not issue FIRC)
Export ordinary VAT invoice or Fully Digitalized E-Invoice for the export sale
Container loading report or customs seal record where applicable
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The STA audits export VAT refunds by cross-matching data from China Customs and SAFE, including customs declarations, foreign-exchange receipts, invoice data, and payment rails. If zero-rating or refund eligibility cannot be substantiated, the STA claws back the refund with late-payment interest and imposes a penalty of 50% to 500% of the tax under the Law on Administration of Tax Collection. Fraudulent export-rebate claims additionally trigger criminal liability under Article 204 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China, with penalties including imprisonment up to life imprisonment and confiscation of property. The WFOE may also be downgraded in tax-credit rating, suspended from export-rebate processes, placed on a customs risk-monitoring blacklist, and subjected to administrative fines.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC); State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) is the delegated foreign-exchange regulator enforcing capital controls and trade administration rules.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: China maintains current-account convertibility for goods, services, profit remittances and dividends under IMF Article VIII, but the capital account remains firmly managed by SAFE. A WFOE may convert registered equity capital into RMB only after obtaining an FDI registration recordal, opening a designated foreign-exchange capital account with a domestic Tier-1 bank, and demonstrating a genuine underlying transaction through invoices, contracts and customs records. Profit remittances are permitted only after annual statutory audit, tax filing, tax clearance and a board resolution; the overseas parent then receives USD or EUR through a bank's standard investment-profits remittance procedure. In practice, operational liquidity is freely convertible, but structural capital transfers, derivative hedging and cross-border financing remain subject to pre-approval or bank recordal. Any round-tripping, speculative currency trading, or use of injected capital for off-scope investments will be blocked or unwound, and the bank must report suspicious use to SAFE under the trade-background principle.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds from the manufacture of high-voltage power transformers must be repatriated to mainland China via a SAFE-monitored domestic bank and entered into the Trade Foreign Exchange Monitoring System within the contractually agreed payment terms, generally no later than 180 days after the date of customs export declaration unless a SAFE extension is granted beforehand. There is no mandatory conversion ratio; the WFOE may retain the proceeds in a foreign-currency settlement account or convert them to RMB at the market rate. All foreign exchange receipts must be matched to genuine customs declarations, commercial invoices, packing lists and transport documents before settlement is accepted. Stand-alone surrender requirements no longer apply, but the full amount must be repatriated, not retained offshore.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: SAFE Foreign Exchange Capital Account plus RMB Basic Deposit Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: RMB Settlement Account with Electronic Tax and Customs Declaration Interface
Foreign Currency Settlement Account and Export Proceeds Collection Account
Documentary Import and Export Settlement Account with Trade Finance Sub-Limit

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low and legally restricted. Offshore digital EMIs such as Wise, Airwallex, Revolut Business and other neobanks are not licensed by the PBOC or SAFE to retain RMB deposits, open domestic corporate accounts, or participate in CIPS and China Financial Gateway clearing for a mainland WFOE. They cannot receive FDI capital as a receiving bank, cannot issue Chinese account numbers, and cannot act as settlement banks in cross-border LCs or trade collections. Their permissible role is limited to front-end foreign-exchange quotation and user interface, with the actual clearing executed by a licensed mainland bank or an offshore correspondent. For this WFOE, fintech EMI onboarding is therefore not a viable substitute for the Tier-1 bank program and is not recommended.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical in-branch attendance is mandatory. At least one statutory director or the authorized financial signatory must appear before the bank's compliance officer for the initial capital-account and RMB basic-account opening; a fully remote consular proxy opening is not accepted by Tier-1 banks in mainland China. The bank will perform a face-to-face interview, compare original passports and residence permits, and require wet-seal signatures on all regulatory declarations. A power of attorney may be executed overseas, but it must be notarized, apostilled or consularized, translated into Chinese by a certified translator, and the attorney-in-fact must be physically present with his or her own identity documents. Post-onboarding, routine transactions can be executed through electronic banking channels.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO concealment through a multi-tier offshore holding chain created to obscure the natural-person owner.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited organizational chart from the ultimate natural-person owner to the WFOE; certificate of incumbency, register of members and shareholder ledger for every intermediate holding vehicle; notarized passport and proof of residential address of the UBO; source-of-wealth statement supported by three years of bank statements and audited financials of the UBO; signed UBO declaration and control attestation on the bank's current-year form.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade mis-invoicing and ghost-shipment risk in high-value power transformer contracts, including inflated unit prices or missing transportation reality.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete transaction file per shipment: signed purchase or sale contract, commercial invoice, packing list, bill of lading or air waybill, China customs declaration number and QR code, manufacturing test certificates for solid-state transformer components, insurance certificate, and where invoice value exceeds the bank's benchmark, a third-party pre-shipment inspection report from SGS, Bureau Veritas or Intertek; bank statement of prior historical trade flows with the same counterparty.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, export-control, military-end-use or politically exposed person exposure associated with the foreign parent, directors, or end-buyers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current World-Check and Dow Jones or Refinitiv sanctions and PEP screening report showing no direct match; passport and biometric residence permit for every director and beneficial owner; PEP self-certification with source-of-wealth if any PEP ownership is declared; overseas sponsor bank reference letter under ICC guidance; signed undertaking to notify the domestic bank within five business days of any regulatory enforcement, sanctions listing or UBO change; export-control end-use statement for all transformer components.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital account injection funds being diverted outside the approved business scope, such as domestic equity investment, entrusted loans, wealth-management products, or out-of-scope property transactions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SAFE FDI registration code and bank-issued capital account settlement record; use-of-proceeds budget board resolution; post-injection payment trail showing each conversion paired with invoices, procurement contracts, payroll registrations and lease agreements; Chinese CPA-issued capital verification report submitted within six months of injection; annual SAFE reconciliation of capital account utilisation; declaration that no portion will be placed in entrusted lending or speculative investments.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The overseas parent remits equity injection via SWIFT MT103 to the WFOE's designated SAFE-recorded Foreign Exchange Capital Account at Bank of China Limited, with field 72 or purpose declaration stating FDI registered capital and equity contribution and the corresponding SAFE BOP purpose code 622. The receiving bank verifies the FDI registration code, entity name in the bank account, and the exact currency and amount against the recorded registered capital. Upon receipt, the WFOE may retain USD or EUR in the foreign-currency capital account or settle into RMB at the prevailing spot rate; settlement must be supported by invoices, purchase contracts, payroll schedules and other genuine transaction documents. A Chinese registered CPA then performs capital verification and issues a formal report, and the bank files the transaction with SAFE within the prescribed reporting window. Funds are ring-fenced for transformer manufacturing working capital and cannot be used for equity investment, entrusted loans, land purchase, or wealth management without SAFE permission.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For imports of silicon steel, copper winding wire, cooling radiators, insulating materials and electrical switchgear components, the WFOE can execute open-account outward remittances via SWIFT MT103 to the overseas supplier after customs clearance, or use a SWIFT MT202 for bank-to-bank cover. For high-value capital equipment purchases, the preferred rail is an irrevocable documentary Letter of Credit issued under UCP600 through the Tier-1 bank, with commercial invoice, packing list, bill of lading and certificate of origin presented; documentary collections D/P and D/A are acceptable only for repeat low-risk counterparties. Where the supplier accepts RMB, settlement should be routed through CIPS using the supplier's CIPS membership identifier, with the WFOE's customs declaration number and trade invoice identifier included in the payment instruction. All outbound payments require matching customs declarations, contract copies, and transport documentation before the compliance release.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable RMB/USD and RMB/EUR forward contracts with genuine trade-backed cash-flow documentation; maturity must match the underlying commercial contract and the hedge cannot exceed the contracted amount.
FX swaps between spot and forward legs for temporary RMB/USD liquidity management during annual profit remittance cycles, limited to operating treasury needs and not for speculative carry trades.

Cross-currency interest rate swaps for long-term USD or EUR capital-structure hedging, approved by the domestic bank under SAFE derivative eligibility rules and marked-to-market through the onshore interbank system.

Zero-cost collar structures combining FX options for current-account hedging, purchased only from a licensed onshore bank; offshore non-deliverable forwards are not permissible for mainland corporate treasuries and are unenforceable in China.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Enterprise Annual Information Report (annual report) filed on the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) through the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System, with information shared with the Ministry of Commerce
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 1 to June 30 each year, covering the immediately preceding fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file within the statutory window places the WFOE on the List of Enterprises with Abnormal Operations; if uncorrected for three consecutive years, the entity is moved to the Serious Illegal and Untrustworthy Enterprise List, which triggers joint disciplinary restrictions and may ultimately lead to administrative revocation of the business license or forced deregistration by SAMR.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Foreign Investment Information Report (foreign investor and actual-controller annual disclosure)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) through the SAMR National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System single-window portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 1 to June 30 each year for the preceding calendar year; the annual report must be completed through the same public credit portal as the enterprise annual report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to report accurately or at all may result in a SAMR/MOFCOM corrective order and an administrative fine of up to RMB 500,000 (approximately USD 70,000); continued non-compliance is published on the credit publicity system, supports inclusion in the abnormal-operations and serious-violation lists, and may contribute to administrative revocation of the business license.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax (CIT) Return and Final Settlement (annual tax reconciliation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Taxation Administration (SAT) local tax office with jurisdiction over the WFOE registered address
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual CIT final settlement return is due by May 31 of the following calendar year; quarterly CIT prepayment returns are due within 15 days after each calendar quarter-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing attracts a daily late-payment surcharge of 0.05% of the unpaid tax under the PRC Tax Administration Law; fines of up to 50% of the tax amount (and up to 100% for evasion or false reporting) may be imposed; prolonged arrears or non-filing can lead to tax enforcement seizures, restriction of the legal representative, and tax authority-supported administrative deregistration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value-Added Tax and other turnover-tax returns (VAT, urban construction tax, education surcharges and related periodic filings)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Taxation Administration (SAT) local tax office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: VAT and turnover-tax returns are due on or before the 15th day of the month following a monthly filing period, or on or before the 15th day of the month following the quarter-end for quarterly VAT filers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing or underpayment triggers the statutory daily 0.05% overdue surcharge and administrative fines under the Tax Administration Law; repeat violations may cause VAT invoice restrictions, export refund suspension, asset seizure, and a regulatory recommendation that the market administration revoke the business license.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statement Audit by a Licensed Chinese CPA Firm
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Independent certified accounting firm appointed by the shareholders; the audited financial statements are kept at the registered office and underpin the SAMR annual report and CIT final settlement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Audit must be completed and financial statements approved before the May 31 CIT final settlement deadline; in practice the audit is finalized by April 30 of the following year for shareholder approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to have the annual financial statements audited is a breach of the PRC Company Law and can cause SAMR and tax authorities to reject the annual report and annual tax return; the WFOE may be fined, its credit rating impaired, and its business license revoked if the audit obligation remains uncorrected.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Labor Security Inspection and Social Insurance Contribution Base Declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local Human Resources and Social Security Bureau (HRSS) and, where collection has been transferred, the local tax authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual labor security inspection is normally conducted between January and June of the following year; social insurance contribution-base adjustment is declared annually, commonly applying from July of each year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to pass the labor security inspection or to declare the correct social insurance base may result in correction orders, fines for refusal to cooperate, back-contribution assessments with late-payment surcharges, labor-security violation record publication, and restrictions on government projects, export incentives and business licensing.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: The legal threshold is effectively zero: under the PRC Company Law, every limited liability company, including a WFOE with zero minimum capital, must prepare annual financial statements and have them independently audited by a licensed CPA firm, regardless of balance-sheet size, turnover or headcount. Thus any positive balance-sheet asset balance, any operating turnover, or any employee headcount triggers the audit mandate; there is no small-enterprise audit exemption for a WFOE. Additional quantitative audit triggers arise only in regulated overlay categories such as securities listing, where CSRC and stock-exchange rules impose minimum net profit, revenue and asset thresholds for mandatory independent audits, and in financial-institution supervision, where balance-sheet and turnover thresholds determine the audit regime.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: PRC Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises (ASBE/CAS), which are substantially converged with IFRS, are the governing framework for the WFOE statutory financial statements; the PRC Small Enterprise Accounting Standards are not a general WFOE exemption when investors, lenders or the foreign parent require full CAS or IFRS-comparable reporting. The tax authority also requires CIT annual returns to be prepared on the CAS basis, and the annual audit report must be issued in accordance with PRC auditing standards.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The PRC does not maintain a standalone public UBO register in the EEA sense. Instead, the WFOE must disclose actual-controller and ultimate beneficial ownership information in the annual Foreign Investment Information Report filed between January 1 and June 30 through the SAMR/MOFCOM single-window system; any shareholding transfer, change of foreign investor, or change of actual control must additionally be filed with SAMR for amendment registration within 30 days after the change occurs and reported through the Foreign Investment Information Reporting system within the same 30-day deadline. The annual confirmation is embedded in the free annual report; no separate government UBO filing fee is charged. Failure to comply with the 30-day reporting window for a shareholding transfer or actual-controller change triggers administrative fines, credit-punishment listing, and potential revocation of registration for the entity and directly responsible personnel.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors, Supervisors and Senior Management Officers
Register of Charges and Mortgages over registered assets
Minute Book of shareholders meetings and board meetings
Statutory accounting books, vouchers, ledgers and financial statements

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,200 to USD 3,500 per annum for a licensed corporate-services or registered-address arrangement in a first-tier city; direct physical office lease costs are excluded from this market range
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,000 to USD 8,000 per annum for a standard WFOE audit performed by a licensed Chinese CPA firm, with complexity-based increases for multi-

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Preferential 15% rate for High and New Technology Enterprises (HNTE) meeting statutory criteria; 100% additional super deduction for qualified R&D expenses; accelerated depreciation for fixed assets, and reduced rate for encouraged industries in Western China (15%).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form A100000 (Corporate Income Tax Annual Return – General) together with applicable schedules; filed via the State Taxation Administration's e-Tax Bureau online portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual settlement after quarterly provisional filings
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Annual return must be filed and tax settled within 5 months after the fiscal year-end (i.e., by 31 May). Quarterly provisional returns due within 15 days after each quarter-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total revenue (operating income) from main operations and other operations
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a WFOE, report revenue in RMB as accrued under PRC GAAP. Cross-border sales to related parties must be identified and arm's length adjustments disclosed; transfer pricing penalties may apply if intercompany pricing deviates.

Deduct cost of goods sold including raw material imports from related parties. Ensure that customs valuation and transfer pricing records support the amounts; unsupported costs may be re-characterized.
Includes urban construction tax, education surcharges, and local education surcharges based on VAT paid. Non-resident treaty relief is irrelevant to this line.
Report marketing and distribution costs. For an exporter, international freight and insurance need proper invoicing; related-party agent fees must pass arm's length scrutiny.

Include management fees, head office cost allocations. China requires a documented cost-sharing agreement; head office general expenses deductible only up to statutory limits. For WFOE, payments to foreign headquarters for services must meet beneficial ownership and substance tests.

Interest on intercompany loans from non-resident shareholders must comply with thin capitalization rules (debt-equity ratio 2:1 for non-financial enterprises). Excess interest is non-deductible and may be reclassified as dividends.
Impairment on trade receivables from related parties must be evidenced; China does not allow deduction for general bad debt provisions, only specific write-offs.
Derived from statutory books. Ensure no non-creditable input VAT is capitalized incorrectly; all foreign exchange gains/losses recognized if functional currency is RMB.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: Article 62 of PRC Tax Administration Law (TAL) – up to RMB 2,000 fine for ordinary non-compliance; RMB 2,000–10,000 for serious. Late payment: daily surcharge of 0.05% of the overdue tax. Fraudulent understatement: Article 63 TAL defines tax evasion – 50%–500% of the underpaid tax as penalty; if criminal, Article 201 of Criminal Law imposes up to 7 years imprisonment.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% on dividends paid by a resident enterprise to a non-resident enterprise (unless reduced by a tax treaty).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim DTA relief, the non-resident shareholder must file 'Information Form for Non-Resident Taxpayers Claiming Treaty Benefits' (SAT Bulletin 2015 No. 60) with the withholding agent before dividend distribution. The shareholder must provide a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from its jurisdiction, and substantiate beneficial ownership over the shares. The WFOE must withhold the reduced rate only after the procedures are followed; otherwise statutory 10% applies. The form is a 'self-assessment' – the payer retains documents for 10 years (prudent practice).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory WHT on royalties and interest is 10% each for non-resident enterprises. Under China's tax treaties, interest WHT may be reduced to 5% or 0%, royalty WHT to 5% (or 6% depending on treaty), but strict beneficial ownership and TRC documentation is mandatory.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: RMB 200 million total related-party tangible asset transactions; RMB 100 million related-party intangible asset or financial asset transactions; RMB 40 million for other related-party transactions in aggregate (per SAT Bulletin 2016 No. 42).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: China does not maintain a separate Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) regime as in offshore hubs; however, the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR) under Article 47 of the EIT Law and SAT Bulletin 2012 No. 7 allow recharacterization of transactions lacking commercial substance. A WFOE must have actual employees, premises, equipment, and core income-generating activities (CIGA) within China for manufacturing; otherwise, tax benefits may be denied and withholding taxes imposed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion – Underreporting Income / Inflating Costs
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly filing a CT return omitting export revenue from the sale of solid-state transformers to related foreign distributors and recording fake import invoices for raw materials to reduce taxable profit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 63 of the PRC Tax Administration Law imposes recovery of unpaid tax plus a penalty of 50%–500% of the tax evaded; failure to pay may trigger a tax lien and asset seizure.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: If the evasion is committed by the company, the courts may pierce the corporate veil where the director personally directed or actively participated. Under Article 20 of PRC Company Law and tax case precedent, directors can be jointly liable for restitution of the tax loss. Travel bans and exit restrictions are imposed under Article 12 of the Exit-Entry Administration Law; criminal conviction under Article 201 of the Criminal Law may lead to up to 7 years' imprisonment and fines.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Misstatement – Failure to Maintain or Submit Documentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: A WFOE contracts intercompany sales of transformers to a Hong Kong affiliate at a price below cost, shifting profit offshore, and fails to prepare Local File or timeliness file under SAT Bulletin 2016 No. 42.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 44 and 45 of the EIT Law, tax authorities may make transfer pricing adjustments, impute interest on the resulting adjustment, and impose a 5% per annum penalty (surcharge) on the underpaid tax. The related party adjustment rules in Bulletins 2016 No. 42 and 2017 No. 6 also provide for a 50%-500% penalty for incomplete or false documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign the TP documentation or knowingly implement pricing without arm's length analysis may be personally assessed for the secondary liability. In egregious cases, the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (Article 47) allows recharacterization, and the director's personal assets may be vulnerable to satisfaction of tax claims if the company's structure is deemed a sham. Criminal exposure for tax evasion may arise if the adjustment leads to tax underpayment exceeding RMB 50,000 and 10% of the declared tax.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance Facilitating Cross-Border Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE merely holds intangible property (designs of solid-state transformers) on paper without any Chinese employees, R&D activities, or manufacturing operations, and licenses royalties to related offshore entities, while claiming treaty benefits as a resident enterprise.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR under Article 47 EIT Law and SAT Bulletin 2017 No. 6 allow disregarding the legal form and recharacterizing income. Unilateral anti-avoidance provisions in the tax treaty (e.g., Limitation on Benefits provisions) may deny treaty benefits. Penalties under Article 123 TAL for false reporting; the tax authority can adjust taxable income and impose a 50%-500% penalty.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the shell entity risk personal liability for abuse of corporate form; Chinese courts may apply 'piercing the corporate veil' (Article 20 Company Law) when the WFOE's separate existence is used to escape tax obligations. Personal fines and criminal liability under Article 201 of the Criminal Law for fraudulent tax filings. Moreover, under the Foreign Investment Law and associated regulations, the enterprise could be blacklisted for serious tax violations, restricting the director's ability to travel into and out of China and managing other enterprises.
